title: Dynamic allocator fallback contracts and testing cookbook
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This cookbook defines machine-readable fallback contracts for the dynamic allocator (service: allocator-api) and a compact, repeatable testing matrix operators and QA engineers can run before, during, and after rollouts. It focuses on preserving critical SLOs (p95 latency, availability) while allowing safe degradation of non-critical tenants. The guide codifies:

- The contract language (edges, invariants, and signals).
- A prioritized test matrix across failure modes (capacity pressure, kernel faults, network partitions, API throttles).
- Operator playbook for controlled experiments and emergency rollback.
- CI harness examples and CLI recipes for local reproduction.

Context and goals
-----------------
Problem: allocator-api routes multi-tenant inference requests across GPU pools using heuristics and capacity credits. Real-world failure modes (e.g., stale capacity view, preemption, cross-tenant KV-cache thrash) have previously caused opaque evictions that violated premium-tenant p95 SLOs.
Goals:

1) Define deterministic fallback behaviors that are testable and observable.
2) Provide a small set of gates and test cases to verify the contract before enabling a rollout flag.
3) Ensure operator safety: human-in-loop thresholds, automated rollback triggers, and clear owner responsibilities.

Contract definitions (human readable + machine hints)
---------------------------------------------------
Contract v1.2 (summary):

- Primary invariant: premium-tenant p95 <= 120ms for steady-state traffic; when this cannot be met, allocator-api must fall back to model-variant-routing (cheaper, lower-memory variants) rather than evicting active premium work.
- Secondary invariant: best-effort tenants may be queued or soft-evicted but must not exceed a 30s retry window before a hard reject.
- Capacity view staleness threshold: if capacity snapshot age > 7s, switch to conservative allocation mode (no preemption, use overflow pool).
- Safety cutoff: if global GPU utilization > 91% for 15s, start throttling new best-effort requests and set telemetry tag allocator.fallback=throttle.

Contract fields (machine-binding):
- decision_priority: [premium, standard, best_effort]
- fallback_action: [model_variant_swap, queue_soft, throttle_new, hard_reject]
- max_queue_time_secs: integer
- staleness_threshold_secs: integer
- trigger_metrics: list of metric expressions (e.g., cpu:gpu_utilization>0.91@15s, kv_cache_miss_rate>0.12@30s)

Testing matrix (owner: allocator-test-team)
-----------------------------------------
Run each test in the matrix in an isolated stage environment with the same operator flags used for the target rollout. Tests are ordered by importance.

1) Capacity-pressure happy path\   Purpose: validate model_variant_swap before eviction\   Steps: create steady premium stream (1k rps), inject burst of best-effort 3x baseline until GPU util reaches 88%-92%.\   Expected: premium p95 stays <=120ms; best-effort requests enter soft queue, queue depth <= configured max_queue_time_secs.

2) Stale snapshot scenario\   Purpose: validate conservative allocation switch\   Steps: block capacity-updater updates (simulate 10s pause) while load remains steady.\   Expected: allocator logs "conservative-mode"; no preemptions; routing uses overflow pool; premium p95 impact < 15% relative.

3) Prefetch-KV thrash\   Purpose: detect high KV miss cascade leading to latency spikes\   Steps: create many short-seq requests to blow KV cache working set.\   Expected: trigger kv_cache_miss_rate metric; allocator sets fallback_action=model_variant_swap for affected tenants; emit event allocator.kv_thrash_alert.

4) Preemption and eviction safety\   Purpose: ensure preemption never targets premium in fallback window\   Steps: force spot eviction on a GPU host; monitor eviction candidates.\   Expected: eviction list excludes premium-tagged tasks unless operator override.

5) Partitioned control plane\   Purpose: ensure safe degradation when control plane connectivity is limited.\   Steps: cut control-plane -> region control messages for 20s while compute nodes remain healthy.\   Expected: nodes switch to local-policy mode; policy logs include last-known-contract-hash; consistency check emits operator-facing summary.

Test matrix table (quick view)
-----------------------------
| Test id | Failure mode         | Expected primary fallback     | Key metric to assert      | Owner |
|---------|----------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| T1      | capacity_pressure    | model_variant_swap, throttle  | premium_p95, queue_depth  | allocator-test-team |
| T2      | stale_snapshot       | conservative_mode, no_preempt | capacity_snapshot_age     | allocator-test-team |
| T3      | kv_thrash            | model_variant_swap            | kv_cache_miss_rate        | runtime-team |
| T4      | host_preempt         | exclude_premium_from_eviction | eviction_candidates       | infra-sim |
| T5      | control_plane_netcut | local_policy_mode             | control_plane_last_seen   | allocator-test-team |

Operator runbook (when a test fails in staging or during canary)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Triage: check dashboard `allocator-contracts/canary` for failing asserts and tagged events (allocator.fallback_*).
2) If premium_p95 is breached > 20% from baseline for > 3m: immediately disable new traffic to the canary cohort via feature-flag `alloc.canary.accept=false` and notify on-call.
3) If queue_depth exceeds configured max_queue_time_secs for > 90s: flip `alloc.queue_backoff=aggressive` and open mitigation ticket.
4) For control plane partition symptoms: promote operator to runbook step `promote-local-mode` which sets `alloc.enforce_local_policy=true` and runs `allocatorctl reconcile --grace 60s` to ensure node-local decisions.
5) Escalation: if human intervention fails within 10m and premium SLOs remain violated, trigger rollback to previous allocator release: `deployctl rollback allocator-api --tag vX.Y.Z` and follow regional failover procedure.

Rollout checklist (pre-merge + pre-flag)
---------------------------------------
- [ ] Contract unit tests added (CI target: allocator-contracts-suite).
- [ ] Integration harness test T1..T5 passing in staging for 2 sequential runs.
- [ ] Canary cohort defined (5% traffic, non-overlapping high-value tenants).
- [ ] Observability: dashboards created under `allocator-contracts/canary` and alerts configured (see Alert rules below).
- [ ] Operator playbook attached to the feature flag UI with run link to this doc.

Alert rules (samples)
--------------------
- alert: AllocatorPremiumP95Spike
  expr: increase(allocator_p95_premium[3m]) > 0.20
  for: 3m
  severity: page
  runbook: "See Operator runbook -> triage"

- alert: AllocatorQueueDepthHigh
  expr: allocator_queue_depth_seconds{queue_type="best_effort"} > 30
  for: 2m
  severity: ticket

- alert: AllocatorSnapshotStaleness
  expr: max_over_time(capacity_snapshot_age[1m]) > 7
  for: 30s
  severity: page

CI / local test harness examples
--------------------------------
- Local harness uses `alloc-sim` and synthetic traffic generator `simgen`. Example:

# Run T1 locally (bash)
simgen --premium-rps 1000 --best-effort-rps 3000 &
alloc-sim --profile staging --inject-burst 3x --target-gpu-util 0.9 

- Contract unit test sample (pseudo-yaml)
---
contract_id: c01
decision_priority: [premium, standard, best_effort]
staleness_threshold_secs: 7
max_queue_time_secs: 30
triggers:
  - expr: gpu_utilization>0.91@15s
    action: throttle_new
---

Observability and dashboards
---------------------------
Create a focused dashboard `allocator-contracts/canary` with these tiles:
- premium_p95 time-series (baseline overlaid)
- queue depth by tenant_class
- capacity_snapshot_age gauge
- eviction_candidates list (last 30m)
- allocator.fallback.* event stream (recent 100)

Ownership, SLAs and handoffs
----------------------------
- Primary owner: allocator-api team (oncall pager: @allocator-oncall).
- Test harness ownership: allocator-test-team.
- Runtime mitigations: runtime-team.
- SLA expectations: allocator-api must preserve premium p95 <=120ms 99.9% of the time in steady-state. Any change to these numeric targets requires product sign-off and a new contract version published in this doc.

Postmortem and retrospective guidance (if an incident occurs)
------------------------------------------------------------
1) Within 48 hours: produce a short incident timeline and attach failing asserts and test reproducer artifacts to the postmortem.
2) Within 7 days: run a contracted test suite with production-like traffic and publish results to `eng-platform/retrospectives/allocator-contract-breaks-YYYY`.
3) Actionable outputs: either tighten the contract (smaller staleness threshold, lower throttles) or add compensating operator tooling (e.g., automatic warm-up for overflow pool).

Appendix A: quick CLI recipes
-----------------------------
# Check contract hash across nodes
allocatorctl verify-contract --contract-id c01 --until 60s

# Force conservative switch on region (operator only)
allocatorctl set-mode --region eu-west-1 --mode conservative --reason "test"

# Reconcile local decisions after network blip
allocatorctl reconcile --grace 60s --dry-run=false

Appendix B: examples of synthetic failure scripts
------------------------------------------------
- capacity_burner.py (python): script that progressively increases best-effort load while recording metrics to prometheus.
- kv_thrash_sim.sh (bash): starts 1k short-L prompt workers to drive KV miss rate.

Document history and governance
-------------------------------
- v1.0 2026-04-05: initial draft by Avery Chen.
- v1.1 2026-09-13: added kv_thrash test (Sara Patel).
- v1.2 2026-11-02: tightened staleness threshold and added snapshot assertions.
- v1.3 2027-01-15: added rollback playbook, updated alerts (reviewers: Diego Morales, Joon Kim).

If you are adding a new automated test or modifying the contract, update the contract YAML examples in `infra/allocator/contracts/` and tag a CI artifact with `contract-hash:<sha>` so we can correlate test runs with deployed behavior.
